identity.title: RoboMME: Benchmarking and Understanding Memory for Robotic Generalist Policies

problem.claim: Evaluate memory for VLA models in long-horizon, history-dependent robotic manipulation tasks.

gap.claim: Existing evaluations use narrow, non-standardized settings, limiting systematic understanding, comparison, and progress measurement.

contributions.claim: Introduces RoboMME, a large-scale standardized benchmark with 16 manipulation tasks covering temporal, spatial, object, and procedural memory.
Develops 14 memory-augmented VLA variants based on the π0.5 backbone, spanning multiple memory representations and integration strategies.
Reports that memory-representation effectiveness is highly task-dependent, with different designs showing distinct advantages and limitations.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present RoboMME as a standardized benchmark and pair it with a systematic suite for comparing memory representations across integration strategies.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that memory-representation effectiveness varies substantially by task, and that each design has different advantages and limitations.

narrative_sequence.summary: Long-horizon manipulation requires memory for repeated-action counting and temporarily occluded objects.
VLA memory evaluations are described as narrow and non-standardized, restricting systematic comparison and progress measurement.
RoboMME addresses this with 16 taxonomy-based tasks evaluating temporal, spatial, object, and procedural memory.
The paper adds 14 π0.5-based memory-augmented VLA variants and reports task-dependent differences among memory designs.

source_observation.claim: The abstract organizes the benchmark around a taxonomy of four memory types and separately varies memory representations and integration strategies.

lessons.interpretation: Separating capability dimensions from implementation choices can make comparisons more diagnostic than using a single aggregate task set.
lessons.application: For a new benchmark, define an explicit capability taxonomy, then cross it with controlled system-design variants to expose where each design helps or fails.
lessons.exception: This structure may be unsuitable when the task domain lacks stable, independently meaningful capability dimensions or when factorial comparisons are infeasible.

unknowns: No quantitative scores, baselines, per-task results, or evaluation protocol details are provided.
The abstract does not specify which memory representations or integration strategies are used, nor how the reported task dependence is measured.
